title: PRD: Per-tenant burst-window SLA with hysteresis-based rollback and circuit-breaker thresholds
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Background: High-volume tenants occasionally produce short bursts that cause p95/p99 latency spikes and rapid error-budget consumption. Existing global SLOs do not distinguish short burst behaviour per tenant and lead to noisy rollback decisions. This PRD defines a per-tenant "burst-window" SLA construct with hysteresis to avoid flapping, an associated circuit-breaker policy, and progressive mitigation actions (soft-throttle -> queued-inference -> reroute to warm-standby capacity). Goal: reduce unnecessary global rollbacks during transient spikes while protecting platform SLOs and preventing a single tenant from destabilizing shared capacity.
acceptance_criteria: Define per-tenant SLIs and SLOs: p50/p95/p99 token-latencies measured on a sliding 1m and 5m burst window, and per-tenant error-rate over 5m and 1h windows.
Hysteresis rules implemented: a tenant enters 'degraded' state only if burst-window p95 > threshold for 3 consecutive 1m windows, and exits only after 10m of sustained recovery.

Circuit-breaker thresholds: automatic progressive actions triggered at burst burn rates: (a) soft-throttle 10% at burst-burn-rate 2x baseline, (b) queue-ing at 5x, (c) reroute to warm-standby/dedicated at 10x. Simulated and verified with load tests.
Telemetry and dashboards show per-tenant SLI time series, active-degraded-tenant list, current mitigation action, and cumulative error-budget impact to global SLOs.
Rollout gates: feature rollout behind staged flags (10% tenants -> 30% -> 100%) with automated rollback if global error-budget burn > 20% in 1h or if mean p99 across top 50 tenants degrades > 15%.
Runbook updated with manual escalation steps, customer communication templates for tenants moved to warm-standby or soft-throttled.
Privacy & compliance: no tenant request payloads are stored by new metrics; ensure KMS keys used for any exported logs per Private deployment requirements. Security review completed.
Unit and integration tests for hysteresis logic, circuit-breaker transitions, and routing to warm-standby.
Performance acceptance: mitigation transitions happen within 60s of threshold condition; median extra latency introduced by soft-throttle path < 15ms.
API/Console acceptance: Console exposes per-tenant SLO status and 'opt-out' requests; product team verified UX copy and access restrictions for customer support.
tradeoffs: Conservative hysteresis reduces false positives but delays mitigation for short, severe bursts. Warm-standby routing requires reserved capacity, increasing cost; we propose a hybrid reserved pool sized by 95th-percentile historical burst rate for top 50 tenants. Implementation effort concentrated in the routing and telemetry subsystems; fallback to simpler throttling-only policy if routing integration is delayed.
rollout_gates: Gate 0: Feature flag enabled in staging; run 24h canary tests against synthetic burst profiles.
Gate 1: Enable for 10% of tenants (randomized), monitor error-budget burn and top-50 mean p99 for 48h.
Gate 2: Expand to 30% if Gate 1 stable; require no global error-budget burn > 10% in 1h and no more than 2 unintended tenant degradations per day.
Gate 3: Enable warm-standby routing for high-risk tenants only; verify end-to-end fallbacks from hosted -> dedicated variants.
Gate 4: Gradual 100% rollout once SLIs show stability for 7 days and security review sign-off obtained.
metrics_and_alerting: Per-tenant p50/p95/p99 token-latency (1m and 5m sliding windows).
Burst-burn-rate signal: ratio of current 1m p95 to tenant baseline p95 (baseline computed over trailing 7d excluding known incidents).
Global error-budget burn rate and projected exhaustion time (1h and 24h views).
Alert: 'Tiered-mitigation-failed' if a tenant remains degraded > 60m despite progressive actions.
Alert: 'Canary-burn-excess' triggered during rollout if global error-budget burn > 20% in 1h.
